goal_text: (Reused from research_synth_014) Analyze the three main mechanisms by which the Marshall Plan (1948-1952) contributed to Western European economic recovery.
ground_truth: The Marshall Plan rebuilt Western Europe through three mechanisms: (1) capital injection — approximately $13 billion in grants and loans financed industrial equipment, infrastructure, and raw material imports; (2) trade liberalization — aid was conditioned on reducing intra-European trade barriers, promoting the integration that later became the EEC; (3) technical assistance — productivity missions transferred American management and manufacturing techniques to European industries.
